 Bakom chief urges measured response to forest and land fire issue
 November 19, 2026 22:30 GMT+700 
 Head of Indonesia's Communications Agency (Bakom) Syahganda Nainggolan speaks to the media at the Indonesian House of Representatives (DPR RI) complex in Jakarta on Thursday (Nov. 19, 2026). /ANTARA/Bagus Ahmad Rizaldi. 
 Jakarta (ANTARA) - Head of Indonesia's Communications Agency (Bakom) Syahganda Nainggolan has called for a wise and proportionate response to forest and land fires (karhutla) affecting neighboring countries, including Malaysia, while taking into account the Indonesian government's efforts to tackle the blazes.
Syahganda made the statement in response to reports of a possible Rp57 trillion lawsuit against Indonesia by a former Malaysian official over losses allegedly caused by smoke from forest and land fires.
"First, we must consider that our president has already apologized to Malaysia and Singapore over the recent haze," Syahganda said at the Indonesian House of Representatives (DPR RI) complex in Jakarta on Thursday.
He said President Prabowo Subianto had previously apologized to Malaysia and Singapore for the impact of smoke from forest and land fires, describing the move as part of Indonesia's efforts to maintain good relations with neighboring countries.
Syahganda also highlighted Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's response, in which he expressed appreciation to President Prabowo and the Indonesian government for their efforts to extinguish forest and land fires.
"So Malaysia should follow suit and emulate the graciousness shown by Singapore's prime minister in expressing appreciation," he said.
According to Syahganda, efforts to address forest and land fires should be assessed comprehensively, taking scientific considerations and natural conditions into account.
He expressed hope that the issue would be addressed through mutual understanding and respect for each country's efforts to mitigate the impact of forest and land fires.
